metadata.title: Mednarodna raziskava bralne pismenosti (IEA PIRLS 2021) Nacionalno poročilo – prvi rezultati

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: PIRLS 2021 uses a two-stage cluster sampling design (schools selected first, then intact classes/grades within schools) with probability proportional to size (PPS), so analyses should reflect the complex survey structure when estimating population-representative results. The report presents national and international comparisons for the fourth-grade cohort (and, where applicable, bridge samples for digital vs paper modes), implying that standard PIRLS analysis procedures should be used to obtain correct standard errors and confidence intervals under the sampling design. The manuscript does not specify any particular PIRLS weight variable names (e.g., student design weights) or replicate-weight procedures, so the exact weighting implementation cannot be verified from the text. For practice, analysts should rely on the PIRLS 2021 international database documentation to apply the recommended student weights and variance estimation method consistent with PIRLS scaling and reporting conventions.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: This national report primarily summarizes PIRLS 2021 results (scale scores, international benchmarks, and questionnaire distributions) rather than training or evaluating a predictive model on student-level data. Plausible Values are part of PIRLS achievement scaling, but the report does not document a specific PV-combining strategy for any ML pipeline, and it does not present a missing-data handling method for an empirical predictive analysis. Therefore, PV and missing-data handling are treated as not reported for the purposes of this extraction because the document is descriptive/reporting-focused rather than an ML methods paper.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The report describes PIRLS 2021 as assessing reading literacy in the fourth year of formal schooling (typically fourth grade; some systems used a bridge approach or tested a different grade when the cohort average age was below 9.5 years). Sampling is described as two-stage cluster sampling: schools selected first, then classes/grades within schools, with PPS (probability proportional to size) at the school stage. For Slovenia, the main fieldwork ran between 17 March and 23 June 2021, with participation of 194 schools (332 classes), 6,505 students (5,096 digital PIRLS and 1,409 bridge), 163 principals, 5,974 parents, and 324 teachers. The report also notes PIRLS participation-rate quality guidelines (minimum acceptable participation rates for schools, classes, and students) and that some systems are marked when guidelines were met only after including replacement schools.

data.outcome_summary: This national report presents descriptive PIRLS 2021 results for Slovenia and international comparisons across 57 participating education systems (plus 8 reference participants). PIRLS 2021 measures reading literacy in the fourth year of schooling (typically fourth grade; some systems used a bridge sample to link digital PIRLS to paper-based trend tasks) and uses rotated test booklets (“bundles/zvezki”) so each student answers a subset of reading passages and questions. The report summarizes scale-score comparisons (e.g., Slovenia’s average reading score on the PIRLS scale), international benchmarks (400/475/550/625), and trends between 2016 and 2021, including the observed global decline in 2021. It also reports extensive questionnaire-based context results (home literacy activities, SES gradients, student attitudes toward reading, school climate, and peer harassment), but it does not implement or evaluate any machine-learning predictive model. Consequently, the document’s contribution is policy-relevant interpretation of assessment outcomes rather than ML-based causal or predictive inference.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This is a descriptive national PIRLS reporting document rather than an empirical ML study. As a result, fields related to ML algorithms, PV-combining strategy for a predictive pipeline, and missing-data handling for model estimation are not applicable or not documented in the text. The extraction therefore focuses on assessment design, sampling description, and reported benchmark/scale outcomes, while leaving ML-specific fields empty.
